components.selected_instruction:
Extract explicitly documented diseases, diagnoses, comorbidities, complications and explicitly documented absent/negated conditions of the INDEX PATIENT only. Do not attribute other original patients, literature-review cases, cohort averages, specimen reagents or general recommendations to this patient. Family history belongs in family_genetics, not conditions. Symptoms without a named diagnosis belong in symptoms_function. A transfusion, operation or medication administration is a procedure/treatment, not a disease or complication; extract a complication only when the source names it.

Preserve diagnostic certainty separately from clinical activity and time. Assertion reflects whether the fact is affirmed, negated or uncertain: present, absent, possible, conditional, unknown. Verification_status reflects documented diagnostic certainty: confirmed, provisional, differential, refuted, unconfirmed, unknown. Never infer confirmation from treatment, a billing label, or a symptom alone.

Examples of mapping:
- 'Possible pulmonary embolism' → assertion=possible, verification_status=provisional/unconfirmed.
- 'Pulmonary embolism was excluded / ruled out / no pathology suggestive of thrombosis was observed' → assertion=absent, verification_status=refuted, with a Condition item for the named disease, not for the test.
- 'History of myocardial infarction' → assertion=present, temporality=historical, role=history.
- 'Cancer in remission' → assertion=present, clinical_status=remission.
A differential listed in an educational question is not the answer or a confirmed condition.

Never diagnose from medications, abnormal laboratory values, imaging alone, or recognizable examination clues unless the source itself names the diagnosis. Do not infer CKD stage from creatinine, sepsis from infection/vitals, or tumor stage from metastases. Cancer-specific detail is extracted in the oncology task; preserve the explicit cancer name here without extrapolation.

Set role=primary_diagnosis only when the text explicitly establishes the principal/final diagnosis or reason for the case. Do not force one primary diagnosis for every record. Complications, comorbidities, historical diagnoses, and differentials remain separate. Keep body site, laterality, severity, and stated diagnostic basis when stated. Use the disease name as written, including abbreviations; do not invent SNOMED or ICD codes.

Explicitly named exclusions must be extracted. Do not emit universal negatives from 'review of systems otherwise negative'. Include specifically named exclusions relevant to differential diagnosis or eligibility, e.g., 'no pathology suggestive of thrombosis', 'thrombosis was ruled out', 'no evidence of X'. For these, create a Condition with assertion=absent, verification_status=refuted, name taken verbatim from the source, and evidence quote that contains the negation. Do not expand 'No significant past medical history' into individual disease negatives. 'History unavailable' can establish explicitly_unknown only for that reviewed history scope. Resolved or remitted disease is affirmed historical disease, not refuted.

Preserve distinct episodes and contradictory statements as separate facts when timing differs or cannot be resolved. Evidence must cover the diagnosis and its certainty/negation, not merely a test name elsewhere in the record. The exact quote must occur within the cited segment. Quote table headers and time headings separately when needed; never synthesize a quote joining nonadjacent rows. Only supplied source text supports facts, not target labels or another source format.

TimeMention: use verbatim temporal expression. Never invent dates or durations. date_iso only if YYYY-MM-DD is explicitly present as an unshifted full date; otherwise null. Relation and anchor must reflect explicit anchors such as surgery or admission, not publication date.

Output requirements: all keys required; null/unknown for unstated values. ROOT coverage=complete/limited/not_applicable meaning this task reviewed the supplied source, not that the patient's history is complete. documentation_status=documented includes positive, negative, possible and historical facts; silence is not_documented, never a clinical negative. documentation_evidence is for explicitly_unknown/not_applicable only; fact evidence stays on each item. Empty output is valid when the task has no supported facts. Never instruct skipping difficult fields/facts to pass validation. Preserve schema, source fidelity, patient identity, uncertainty and completeness.

Rewrite the observations extraction strategy to enforce source fidelity, schema compliance and complete clinical recall. Preserve all immutable contracts for schema, source fidelity, patient identity, uncertainty and completeness. Never instruct skipping difficult fields or facts to pass validation. Empty means no supplement.

Scope and fidelity: Extract only measurements and test findings: laboratories, vitals, imaging, pathology, microbiology, physiological tests. Preserve the exact test name, value, comparator < <= > >= =, unit, specimen, method, site, reference interval and time when reported. Do not drop normal quantitative laboratory values merely because they are normal; they may define eligibility or baseline. Do not invent a result from "labs were normal". Record a relevant qualitative finding when explicitly stated. Do not infer abnormality from outside reference ranges; flag=high/low/normal requires wording or an explicit source-provided interval supporting classification. Leave flag=unknown otherwise. Test status and result polarity are separate. 'HIV test negative' is assertion=present, status=resulted, flag=negative. 'No HIV test was performed' is status=not_performed. 'CT ordered to exclude embolism' is ordered, not a negative result. Pending cultures do not establish an organism. A false-positive test described in source must retain that interpretation.

Treatment goals, titration targets and desired therapeutic ranges are NOT measured test results. Do not create an observation for the target alone or mark it resulted. Such targets belong to medication regimen or monitoring plan.

Temporal and repeat handling: Keep repeated values at different times as separate items. Never average, select the most abnormal, convert units, infer eGFR/creatinine clearance, calculate scores, or use publication date as sample date. Preserve '<0.01' rather than replacing with zero. Use text_value when a number or range cannot be safely represented. Distinguish absolute vs percentage counts, plasma/serum/urine specimens, and oxygen settings during a blood gas when written.

Table handling: For measurements in a table, preserve the time from the row-group heading, e.g., On admission versus At 48 h, not merely a general table caption. Include an additional exact quotation of that heading from the SAME table-row segment in the item's evidence so time.text occurs literally in its evidence. Keep the exact data-row quotation as well. Do not concatenate noncontiguous excerpts into a fabricated quotation. Do not erase a documented time to satisfy validation. Keep each patient's column and each time point distinct. For narrative findings, add a separate exact time quotation from that patient's corresponding event when needed. TimeMention.text must be verbatim from source. Relation and anchor must reflect explicit anchors, not publication date. date_iso only if YYYY-MM-DD explicitly present as unshifted full date.

Evidence binding: Evidence should bind the value to the correct test and patient, not merely match the number somewhere in the record. For each evidence quote use the displayed segment ID as source_section. The exact quote must occur within that segment. Quote table headers and time headings separately when needed; never synthesize a quote joining nonadjacent rows. Only supplied source text supports facts, not target labels or another source format. An example in instructions is not patient evidence. Populate only claims supported by supplied record. Empty output is valid when no supported facts exist.

Value representation: Split numeric magnitude, comparator and unit into their fields. Preserve the exact result notation in text_value, including comparators and scientific exponents; keep reference intervals separate. Do not mistake flattened 10^9 for explicit 10^9, convert units, or copy a reference threshold as patient result. For comparator symbols, set comparator to > < >= <= = unknown and keep the original notation in text_value, e.g., text_value '>15', numeric_value 15, comparator '>'. If comparator is present and numeric_value cannot be safely isolated, keep numeric_value null and text_value verbatim.

Absence handling: documentation_status documented includes positive, negative, possible and historical facts. Silence is not_documented, never a clinical negative. For a named test with unstated result use result_absent_reason=not_reported. Pending uses status=pending, result_absent_reason=pending, text_value null, numeric_value null, flag unknown. Not performed uses status=not_performed, result_absent_reason=not_performed. Missing mention produces no item.

Kinds and subjects: Subject must be index_patient/family_member/mother/fetus/newborn/other/unknown. Assertion reflects explicit affirmation, negation or uncertainty, not test positivity. Kind must be laboratory/vital/imaging/pathology/microbiology/physiologic/other. Status must be resulted/ordered/planned/pending/not_performed/historical/unknown. result_absent_reason null when result provided.

Output field guide: ROOT coverage=complete/limited/not_applicable; limitations list[string]; documentation_status documented/not_documented/explicitly_unknown/not_applicable; documentation_evidence list[Evidence] for explicitly_unknown/not_applicable; items list[Observation]. Evidence: quote string, source_section string|null. Observation required keys: subject, assertion, temporality, time, evidence minItems1, result_absent_reason, name, kind, status, text_value, numeric_value, comparator, unit, flag, reference_range_text, specimen, method, body_site. TimeMention required: text, relation, anchor, date_iso.

Do not memorize cases, source IDs or answer values. Do not infer missing results. Keep specimen, value/unit, planned vs performed status and separate encounters. Split named laboratory/immunohistochemical panel members into individual observations. Distinguish performed test from absent finding. Preserve uncertainty and completeness.

Repair by diagnosing clinical omissions, contradictions and schema violations from feedback without changing immutable source/schema/validator contracts. Re-read the task definition, schema, and supplied source text. Compare the previous output to validation errors and feedback to identify missing required items, incorrect assertions, verification status, temporality, role, body site/laterality, time mentions, and evidence support. Never instruct skipping difficult fields or facts to pass validation. Preserve patient identity: extract only facts for the index patient; do not attribute other original patients, literature-review cases, cohort averages, specimen reagents or general recommendations to this patient. Preserve source fidelity: every extracted fact must be supported by an exact contiguous quote from the supplied segments; use the displayed segment ID as source_section; never synthesize quotes across nonadjacent rows. Preserve uncertainty and completeness: map assertion, verification_status, temporality, clinical_status and documentation_status exactly as documented; do not infer diagnoses from medications, labs, imaging or exam clues unless the source names the diagnosis; use unknown/null for unstated values. Keep all schema-required keys present; output a complete parseable object matching the schema with correct types. Empty items list is valid only when the task truly has no supported facts. Do not memorize cases, source IDs or answer values from feedback; use feedback only to guide error types. If structural errors are reported, return a fully compliant JSON object with correct root fields and item fields, not an alternative format.

Rewrite the timeline_completion strategy to prioritize clinical completeness, source fidelity and validation safety over passing checks. Diagnose omissions and contradictions from feedback and repair them without skipping difficult fields.

Scope and identity: Process only the target patient and record_id. Describe only this patient. Never mix facts across patients or cases. Do not memorize case-specific values, source IDs or answer values. Preserve patient identity throughout events, edges and limitations.

Schema fidelity: Output a single patient-timeline/2 object with schema_version, record_id, events, edges, limitations. Keep required fields. Do not invent episodes. Preserve existing unlinked events verbatim including kind, occurrence and times; add missing events and edges instead of dropping prior events. Retain existing fact links and only use fact_ids from the known_fact_ids for this record; empty is allowed.

Evidence and attribution: Every event must have at least one evidence and one attribution_evidence SourceSpan with segment_id and an exact unique quote from the original source. For existing times/evidence, retrieve the full quotes from the original source segments. Times must preserve literal precision. TimeExpression requires text, kind, precision, calendar_value and evidence with exact quotes. Do not use nonliteral paraphrases. Ensure event_time_unknown is avoided by providing a TimeExpression with evidence when a time is stated, otherwise leave times empty. Do not create calendar_value by substitution.

Clinical completeness: Complete a clinically complete partial order using the delivered fact hints and original source. Include important history, presentation, tests, diagnoses, treatments, adverse events, outcomes, follow-up and plans. Distinguish occurred, planned, declined, conditional and unknown. A planned or declined treatment must never become occurred. Do not invent visits, intervals or calendar dates. Leave genuinely ambiguous order unresolved.

Temporal reasoning: The primary goal is relative clinical sequence, not dates. Order the clinical occurrence, not when it was narrated. Do not derive chronology from paragraph order alone. Use before/after edges with offset null when the source establishes order without a duration. Preserve simultaneity only when stated. Events may have times []. Do not mechanically order by kind. Edges must cite evidence that establishes this pair and relation, not just contain a time word. Evidence for edges must support both events and the relation. Avoid timeline_span_unresolved and nonliteral_quote errors by ensuring times and edges have exact quote evidence.

Uncertainty and limitations: Preserve uncertainty and contradictions. Document limitations for mixed case columns, abstract/discussion passages, missing temporal anchors, and qualitative intervals. Do not skip difficult fields/facts to pass validation. If a field is genuinely ambiguous, leave it unresolved and note in limitations.

Quality controls: Never instruct skipping difficult fields/facts to pass validation. Do not derive chronology from paragraph order. Do not merge distinct administrations, assessments or encounters with different stated ages/days. Distinct events with different stated years/ages/days must be separate events even when mentioned in one sentence. Preserve occurrence semantics. Keep month/year offsets in their own units.

splits.scope: Article-group-disjoint, stratified patient-bearing/negative development examples; earlier pilot exposure is not external blinding.

independent_gepa.reward_notice: Finite gold checks and optionally source-grounded model review. Model review is an unadjudicated proxy; structural-only rewards are not clinical accuracy.

instructions.roster: Identify individually described patients in ALL supplied blocks including abstract, discussion, captions and tables. Human and animal patients are allowed. Cohort size, group mean, generic diagram or anonymous dashboard bed is not an individual case. Include a previously published patient only if this article itself reports an individual clinical course; flag prior publication in attribution_limitations and do not merge across articles. Relatives are separate patients only if independently described. Preserve mother/fetus and comparison patient identity. Assign every block to patients, background or unresolved. Shared/mixed blocks may be assigned to multiple patients with explicit limitations. Include case facts in Discussion. Use exact distinguishing identity quotes, literal segment IDs, unknown species if unstated, and null count if uncertain. Do not invent individuals to cover blocks. This task ONLY identifies patients and source blocks. Figure/panel ownership is evaluated separately; do not output a figures field. Captions can support patient identity when explicitly linked. PRIMARY VERSUS CITED: patients contains cases presented as the article’s own clinical cases including explicit follow-up to a previous publication. Cases merely summarized from other publications belong in cited_cases, never patients. Keep exact evidence and known origin_reference_ids or an empty reference list with a limitation when linkage is uncertain. Do not invent citation IDs or merge identities. Validate primary cases independently of optional cited-case links.
instructions.case_context: Identify what kind of material this record contains before any clinical cohort assignment, assessing all blocks. Use supplied source_kind as provenance, not as evidence all text concerns a living patient. Recognize formalin, dissection specimens, donated cadavers, autopsy/anatomy material, in-vitro experiments. Do not turn cadaver status into social history or clinical death outcome. Distinguish autopsy following a described patient’s clinical course from cadaver-only anatomy. Classify single real case report as clinical_case; real EHR summary as clinical_record; educational questions as exam_vignette; explicitly synthetic scenario as synthetic_vignette. Examination vignette is NOT a verified patient encounter. If multiple unrelated index cases are mixed without a clear primary case use multi_patient and multiple_index_patients=true. Relatives in family history do not make a case multi_patient. Mother-and-infant narratives require careful index-subject identification; use limited when ambiguous. index_subject_description should identify case role without a name and quote the source that establishes the subject; keep null when not identifiable. Mark human/nonhuman only when supported. Describe care setting and chief complaint only when stated. Do not infer admitting specialty. subject_state distinguishes person alive at presentation who later died from pre-existing cadaver specimen. Death during described course does not invalidate clinical case. When TARGET_PATIENT_JSON is supplied classify that single selected patient only; set multiple_index_patients=false and use clinical_case or animal. Never count literature review cases as additional index patients.
instructions.demographics: Extract demographics that can safely support cohort filters, preserving exactly what was documented from all blocks. Record age_at_presentation separately from age_at_diagnosis and age_other. Preserve years/months/days and do not convert infant age in months to years. For ranges or approximate ages retain text_value and leave numeric_value null unless a single explicit number is stated. Do not infer age from dates, schooling, family role or appearance. Always include temporal expression or surrounding presentation wording in evidence. '65-year-old male' supports documented_sex='male' only, not sex_assigned_at_birth or gender_identity. Preserve source wording for sex/gender. Do not infer reproductive potential from documented sex. Race, ethnicity, language and gender are extracted only when explicitly documented, never from names, geography, nationality or stereotypes. Do not emit names, addresses or identifiers. Keep numeric_value, written unit and text_value together. Keep separate observations when different points in the clinical course have different ages. Do not select a present-day age for a historical case. Do not transfer age or sex from a family member, mother or comparison patient to the index case. Missing demographic information stays absent from items array, not as a guessed default. If record states only 'an adult' preserve as text_value with numeric_value=null. Contradictory documented sex or age at same time should be retained separately and flagged in limitations. Use literal quotes with segment_id.
instructions.clinical_inventory: Independently inventory ALL clinically relevant features documented for this target patient across all blocks. Do not see or imitate an extraction result. Scan history, symptoms, examinations, differential and confirmed diagnoses, repeated observations/tests with results and specimen, medications with dose/route and changes, devices/procedures, allergies, family/genetics, social context, oncology, pregnancy, plans, complications, response, outcomes and follow-up. Include negative and uncertain findings with their state, and distinct observations at different times. Keep episode_as_documented literal or null; do not invent visits/dates. Preserve quantities/units/reference versus patient result. Exclude other patients, literature cases, aggregate results and general advice. Each feature must cite exact source quotes with segment_id and be assigned one task class: case_context, demographics, conditions, symptoms_function, medications, allergies, procedures_devices, observations, oncology, family_genetics, reproductive_perinatal, social_exposures, outcomes, care_plans. These are unreviewed coverage hypotheses, never newly accepted clinical facts. Ensure literal quoting, patient ownership and no invented clinical content, dates or performed care.

instructions.conditions: Extract explicitly documented diseases, diagnoses, comorbidities and complications of the INDEX PATIENT only. Preserve diagnostic certainty with assertion confirmed/possible/absent/explicitly_unknown and clinical_status when stated e.g., remission. Use disease name as written, keep body site, laterality, severity and stated diagnostic basis. Set role=primary_diagnosis only when source explicitly establishes principal/final diagnosis or reason for case; do not force one. Do not diagnose from medications, labs, imaging or exam clues unless source names the diagnosis. Do not infer CKD stage from creatinine, sepsis from infection/vitals, tumor stage from metastases. Family history belongs to family_genetics, symptoms without a named diagnosis belong to symptoms_function, procedures/treatments are not conditions. Extract a complication only when named. Do not expand 'review of systems negative' or 'no significant PMH' into individual negatives. Preserve distinct episodes and contradictory statements as separate items when timing differs. Evidence must cover diagnosis and certainty, not just a test name. Empty output is valid.
instructions.symptoms_function: Extract patient-reported symptoms, examination signs, functional limitations, mental status and explicitly reported performance/QOL scores for the INDEX PATIENT. Distinguish patient-reported from observed signs when source permits. Preserve onset, duration, severity, body site, triggers and activity context. Capture mobility, ADLs, dependence, oxygen-related limits, cognition, consciousness and stated ECOG, Karnofsky, GCS, NIHSS or other scores exactly as written; do not calculate scores. Do not convert a symptom constellation into a syndrome or definitive diagnosis. Do not transfer a relative’s symptoms or disability to the index patient. Symptoms from hypothetical differentials or discussion are not extracted. Keep historical, recovered and current deficits temporally distinct. Use numeric_value only when explicitly written, text_value for qualitative descriptions. Quantitative vitals and laboratory tests belong to observations, not duplicated here. Include meaningful explicit negatives with supporting evidence. Missing reporting does not establish normal function. Empty output is valid.
instructions.observations: Extract clinically usable measurements and test findings for the INDEX PATIENT: laboratories, vitals, imaging, pathology, microbiology and physiological tests. Preserve exact test name, value, comparator < <= > >= =, unit, specimen, method, site, reference interval and time when reported. Keep normal quantitative values. Do not invent results from 'labs were normal'. Record qualitative findings when explicitly stated. Flag high/low/normal only if source wording or provided interval supports it; otherwise flag unknown. Test status and result polarity are separate: HIV test negative is resulted flag negative; no test performed is status not_performed; ordered test is not a result. Keep repeated values at different times as separate items; never average, convert units, infer eGFR/creatinine clearance or calculate scores. Preserve '<0.01' exactly. For table measurements include an exact quotation of the row-group heading e.g., 'At 48 h' and the data row in evidence so time.text occurs literally. Keep patient columns and time points distinct. Do not transform an imaging impression into a diagnosis. Evidence must bind value to test and patient. Empty output is valid.
instructions.family_genetics: Extract family disease history and explicit genetic test/inheritance facts with precise subject attribution. Family_member items retain relationship, age at diagnosis, maternal/paternal lineage, gene/variant, inheritance and interpretation when stated. Multiple affected relatives are distinct items. A broad 'family history unremarkable' is not expanded; a named negative family history may be assertion=absent. Genetic tests in the index patient have subject=index_patient; distinguish somatic vs germline only when stated. Do not infer carrier status, penetrance, syndromic diagnosis or hereditary cancer from pedigree. VUS is not pathogenic; a negative test does not exclude all genetic disease. Preserve HGVS-like strings and gene names exactly. Do not transfer fetal/newborn genetic results to mother; use explicit subject labels and note ambiguity. Record consanguinity/inheritance only as stated. Screening recommendations based on family risk are plans, not results. Evidence must establish both the relative or test subject and the clinical/genetic fact. Do not include literature comparisons as family members. Empty output is valid.

instructions.medications: Extract drugs and pharmacologic regimens documented for the index patient. Distinguish action: prescribed/ordered/planned vs administered vs held vs current/home vs conditional. Do not treat review, hypothetical options or discussion mentions as patient exposures. Preserve name/abbreviation exactly; do not expand acronyms or brands unless ingredients are written. Record dose_text as stated; populate numeric dose/unit only when explicit and unambiguous. Preserve route, frequency, duration, indication, regimen when stated; do not assume oral, once daily, standard dose or duration. Prescription amount is not administered dose. Dose changes at different times are separate items. Distinguish medication effects from allergies; adverse reactions go to allergies. Do not assign diagnosis from drug receipt. Capture contrast agents, anesthetics, transfusion products when administered to a clinical patient; exclude specimen preservatives. Retain start/stop/hold context and evidence. Explicit negative e.g., 'takes no medications' is one scoped absent statement with action=unknown; missing list = items=[] not_documented. Empty output is valid.
instructions.allergies: Extract explicitly documented allergies, intolerances and adverse drug effects for the index patient without conflating categories. Capture substance, category, reported reaction, reaction type and severity only when stated. Do not reclassify using outside reasoning; use unknown when source does not distinguish allergy vs intolerance. Do not infer drug-class allergy from one agent. Explicit 'no known drug allergies' is substance='drug allergies', category=drug, assertion=absent; not empty array. Missing documentation = no items, not NKDA. Preserve remote reactions and uncertain attribution; assertion=possible for 'possible rash'. Family member allergy is not patient allergy. Separate events when severity/timing differs; do not erase prior reaction due to later NKDA; flag conflict in limitations. Negative skin test is observation, not proof of absence. Evidence must include reaction/denial and substance when available. Do not invent severity, onset, mechanism or codes. Empty output is valid.
instructions.care_plans: Extract explicitly stated future care actions, referrals, monitoring, counseling and goals-of-care for the index patient. A plan is not a completed action. Distinguish recommended, planned, scheduled, declined, conditional and unknown status; do not imply fulfillment. Include target condition/test, responsible specialty, urgency and temporal instruction only when stated. Do not infer specialist from diagnosis. Conditional escalation requires assertion=conditional with condition in evidence. Do not duplicate full dosing/procedure content from medications/procedures tasks; retain distinct monitoring/referral components. Do not extract standard practice discussions, author recommendations or educational 'next step' questions. Routine discharge advice is extracted only as documented. DNR is goals-of-care, not death. Bind plan to correct patient and timeframe. Explicit negative 'no further follow-up planned' is one source-supported negative plan. Missing plan = items=[] not_documented. Empty output is valid.
instructions.reproductive_perinatal: Extract pregnancy, obstetric, fetal, neonatal, fertility and lactation facts with strict subject separation. Capture explicitly documented pregnancy status, gravidity/parity wording, gestational age, delivery type, loss, live birth/stillbirth, neonatal course, congenital findings, fertility history and lactation. Do not infer pregnancy or absence from age, sex, medications or procedure. Negative pregnancy test is an observation, not timeless never-pregnant status. Preserve gestational age and birth weight as written text with unit; do not convert to decimal weeks. gestational_age_weeks only for explicit single numeric week. Gravidity/parity copied verbatim. Index patient may be mother, fetus or newborn; label other subjects and preserve relationships. Do not merge maternal, fetal and infant data. Multiple fetuses/infants require clear attribution; mark limited if ambiguous. Anatomical specimen findings do not become current complications in unrelated patient. Retain uncertainty, timing and explicit outcomes including termination, loss, neonatal death. Missing history = items=[] not_documented. Empty output is valid.

instructions.oncology:
Extract a patient-owned tumor record from source text only. Create one entry per distinct explicitly described primary malignancy or suspected tumor, assign local IDs t1, t2. Metastases are sites of the same primary unless a separate primary is explicitly established. Exclude family members, benign lesions, non-neoplastic abnormalities, generic risk, or inferred malignancy. Use certainty possible for suspected cancer and absent for explicit exclusions.
Preserve primary site, histology, grade, laterality, disease extent as stated; use unknown if not localized. Keep initial imaging localization separate from later pathology origin; prefer documented final origin and note conflicts. Stage GROUP, TNM, SYSTEM, edition, context are separate fields; do not calculate stage, infer stage IV from metastasis, or reinterpret edition. Clinical and pathologic stage may differ.
Biomarkers retain test/marker name, gene, alteration, assay, specimen, value/unit, interpretation. Distinguish somatic vs germline; VUS is not pathogenic. Link tumor_ref only when source ties result to that tumor. Treatments capture explicitly stated modality, status given/planned/stopped, line, intent, setting neoadjuvant/adjuvant/maintenance, reported response without inference. Empty tumors, biomarkers, treatments are valid when unsupported. Do not infer line, intent, RECIST, remission from drug choice or shrinkage.
instructions.procedures_devices:
Extract explicitly documented procedures, devices and nonpharmacologic therapies with real execution status for the index patient only. Completed surgery/biopsy/intubation differs from order, recommendation, declined or cancelled. Scheduled is planned, not completed; status post is historical completed. A device may be present without implantation date.
Include surgery, invasive diagnostic procedures, dialysis, ventilation support, rehabilitation, radiotherapy procedures, pacemakers, catheters, prostheses, assistive devices when documented. Record body site, laterality, indication, findings, complications only when stated. Distinguish device from the procedure that placed or removed it.
Do not infer procedure from scar, medication, or standard of care. Do not transfer procedures between mother/fetus/newborn or cases. Imaging results belong to observations. Keep timing, negation, uncertainty, cancellation. Evidence must contain action verbs such as underwent, planned, declined, removed, remained in place and identify subject. Empty items is valid when no procedure/device is mentioned.
instructions.outcomes:
Extract explicit clinical-course events for the index patient, not recommendations or hypotheticals. Distinguish improvement, recovery, deterioration, recurrence, readmission, complications, discharge, follow-up, loss to follow-up, death. Preserve related condition, disposition, explicitly documented cause, time anchor and follow-up duration.
Discharged stable is not cured. No recurrence at six months is absent recurrence at that follow-up only. Planned follow-up is care plan, not observed outcome. Death must be an event in the index patient’s described course; exclude relatives, cadavers, general mortality statements, specimens.
Do not calculate overall survival, PFS, time to treatment, censoring dates or causal effects. Do not assume last mention is end of observation. Censoring/loss to follow-up recorded only when explicitly described. Treatment preceding improvement does not prove causality without explicit attribution. Keep progression/response assessments and different follow-up times separate. Missing outcomes yield empty items, not favorable assumptions. Use event=other with precise text for broader states.
instructions.social_exposures:
Extract explicitly documented behavioral, occupational, environmental and social circumstances relevant to cohort definition for the index patient. Separate current, former, never, passive exposure, unknown. Former smoker quit ten years ago is historical, not current. Never-smoker is status=never with assertion present when affirmed; do not infer never from silence.
Preserve substance type, amount, frequency, duration, route and time as stated in amount_text. Pack-years only when explicitly written. Capture alcohol/substance use without adding use-disorder diagnosis. Toxicology screen alone is observation, not pattern. Preserve patient-reported uncertainty and source attribution. Medication administration is not illicit use.
Include occupation/exposures, travel, diet/exercise, housing, food insecurity, social support, access barriers, relevant sexual history when documented. Do not infer socioeconomic status, race, education, adherence from proxies. Do not collect addresses, employer names or contact details. Include exact supporting text for exposures and meaningful named negatives; do not expand social history noncontributory into blanket normality. Empty is valid when unsupported.

instructions.coverage_audit: Compare each numbered inventory hypothesis against the original source and extracted facts. Cover every inventory_index exactly once. Mark represented only when fact IDs preserve all clinical details: polarity, patient, specimen, result/unit, episode and time. Sharing a disease/test name alone is insufficient. A feature represented only under another task class is uncertain, not same-domain coverage; retain its fact IDs for explicit cross-domain review. Mark missing, uncertain or wrong_patient_inventory when appropriate. Inventory and extracted facts can both be wrong. Do not add or erase facts. Assess scope of each claim across abstract, discussion, captions and tables; do not exclude whole sections. This is an unadjudicated coverage review feeding coverage_repair.
instructions.coverage_repair: Repair coverage gaps identified by audit using source-only evidence for the index patient. Preserve exact names, values and wording; do not expand acronyms/brands, convert units, assume oral route, once-daily frequency, standard dose or duration. Distinguish performed/administered from prescribed/ordered/planned/conditional/held/current-home. Record dose_text verbatim; populate numeric dose/unit only when explicit and unambiguous. Keep separate items per distinct time, dose change or administration. Do not treat review, hypothetical, answer-option or alternative-treatment discussion as patient exposure. Retain start/stop/hold context and evidence. Do not infer oncology intent, ingredients, adherence or abnormality. Empty output is valid when no supported facts. Output feeds claim_audit.
instructions.claim_audit: Independently audit EACH listed fact_id against target patient and original text. Return one decision per fact_id: supported, unsupported, wrong_patient or uncertain. Check negation, uncertainty, specimen/analyte, magnitude, exponent/unit, reference versus result, planned versus performed and encounter/time associations. Tumor laterality is not procedure laterality; provisional imaging location is not final pathology origin; no recurrence is not stated remission; transfusion/treatment is not a diagnosed complication. Positive sensitization does not alone establish clinical allergy. Cite exact segment quotes for positive or contradictory evidence; absent evidence may have evidence=[]. Do not use medical knowledge to fill gaps. List possible missing patient facts per extraction task class with literal evidence as adjudication suggestions only. No prose outside JSON. Audits repair and coverage_repair outputs.
instructions.repair: Extract/repair task-specific clinical facts for the index patient only with strict subject separation. Use source-only evidence; preserve literal phrasing for times, gestational age, doses and outcomes. Keep occurred, planned, conditional and unknown distinct. Never invent encounters, dates or performed care. Preserve uncertainty and contradictions. Distinct administrations, assessments or encounters with different stated years/ages/days remain separate; do not merge successive doses or treatment changes. Planned or declined treatment never becomes occurred. Time phrases must be literal in their own evidence; do not derive chronology from paragraph order. Retain fact_id links only when source supports association. Empty output is valid when no supported facts. Repair output is audited by claim_audit and covered by coverage_audit.

limitations: Finite source-reviewed checklist, not exhaustive clinical accuracy/precision/recall.
Three seeds repeat the same articles; checks are not independent patient samples.
Optimizer-held-out articles have previous pilot exposure, not external blinding.
Main status totals include auxiliary tasks; clinical statuses are separately tabulated.
Output token rates include generated reasoning/answer, retries and auxiliary calls; exclude startup and queue.
Detailed pixel descriptions and clinical interpretation not newly adjudicated in this review.
